name: Genchi Genbutsu
definition: We practice genchi genbutsu... go to the source to find the facts to make correct decisions, build consensus and achieve goals at our best speed.

rows.situation: When a problem is reported from the work
rows.under: Decides from the summary. Does not go.
rows.justRight: Goes to the place, looks at the actual work, and decides from what is there.
rows.over: Moves the office to the floor, and every decision now waits for a personal visit.

rows.situation: When the number and the story disagree
rows.under: Picks whichever is more convenient and moves on.
rows.justRight: Goes to the source of both until they reconcile, then decides.
rows.over: Audits both until the decision window has closed.

rows.situation: When you could send someone else to look
rows.under: Always sends someone else, and the facts arrive pre-interpreted.
rows.justRight: Goes in person for the decisions that depend on seeing, and sends someone when they do not.
rows.over: Insists on seeing every detail personally, and becomes the bottleneck.

rows.situation: When people disagree about what is happening
rows.under: Votes, or picks the most senior account.
rows.justRight: Takes the people who disagree to the source, and lets the facts settle it.
rows.over: Requires a field trip for disagreements that a single measurement would end.

rows.situation: When the decision is needed today
rows.under: Skips the look because there is no time, and the decision is wrong.
rows.justRight: Goes quickly, sees the thing that matters, and decides at the speed the facts allow.
rows.over: Treats going to see as a ritual that cannot be shortened, even when the fact is already in hand.

rows.situation: When the report is already thorough
rows.under: Treats every report as gospel because it is long.
rows.justRight: Reads it, then checks the one claim that would change the decision if it were wrong.
rows.over: Ignores good reports on principle, because nothing counts unless you saw it yourself.
